message.content:
You are analyzing a WordPress plugin project to understand its WordPress integration. The project is at /Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro

Please do the following:
1. Search PHP files in src/ (or inc/, classes/ if src/ doesn't exist) for:
   - `register_rest_route(` calls → extract namespace string from first argument
   - `add_menu_page(` / `add_options_page(` / `add_submenu_page(` calls → extract page slug (last positional argument before the callback)
   - `current_user_can(` calls → extract capability strings (ignore generic ones: manage_options, activate_plugins, edit_posts)
   - Directory names or conditional constants suggesting a free/pro split: IS_PRO, is_pro(), directories named pro/ or free/, separate composer packages
2. Do not read vendor/ or tests/

Return ONLY a JSON object (no other text) with these fields:
{
  "rest_namespace": "/wp-json/<namespace>/<version>/ or null",
  "settings_path": "/wp-admin/admin.php?page=<slug> or null",
  "capabilities": ["<capability-1>"],
  "editions": ["free", "pro"] or null
}

Use null for any field where no clear evidence was found.

- backwpup-architecture: Use this skill when changing service structure, shared logic, bootstrapping, dependency wiring, or any code that may affect FREE/PRO boundaries in BackWPup.
- backwpup-frontend-architecture: Use this skill when changing admin JavaScript, CSS, or HTML templates in BackWPUp Pro.
- sprint-shortlister: Generate a sprint shortlist for wp-media/backwpup-pro with fast story point estimation and capacity planning.

Use this skill whenever you need to:
- Plan a 2-week sprint for BackWPUp Pro with realistic team capacity constraints
- Quickly estimate effort on unstarted issues without full grooming analysis
- Create a balanced shortlist across bugs, features, and tech debt
- Generate a shareable HTML report for sprint planning meetings

The skill asks for team size (default: 2 developers), optionally a target milestone, then fetches open unassigned issues from the repo. It estimates story points through lightweight scope analysis, builds a prioritized shortlist to fit the sprint capacity, and outputs an interactive HTML report ready to share with stakeholders. The entire process takes 2–3 minutes.
- changelog: Generate a changelog entry from merged PRs since the last git tag. Use this when preparing a release, drafting release notes, or summarizing what changed between versions — even if the user says "what changed since last release" or "help me write release notes". Invoke with `/changelog` (since last tag) or `/changelog v3.x.x` (since a specific tag).
- checkout: List all your unread GitHub notifications, grouped by priority and type (mention, review requested, assigned, etc.) with clickable URLs. Use this as a quick daily triage of everything waiting for your attention on GitHub — like checking github.com/notifications but from the terminal. Invoke with `/checkout`.
- estimate: Estimate the complexity of a GitHub issue for sprint planning. Use this whenever someone wants to size a ticket, groom a backlog item, plan a sprint, or get a sense of effort — even if they just say "how big is this?" or "is this a quick fix?". Invoke with `/estimate <issue-number>` or `/estimate <GitHub issue URL>`.
- skill-audit: Audit all Claude skill files for stale references, ambiguous triggers, and hardcoded values. Use this periodically to keep the skill library healthy — invoke with `/skill-audit`. Reports PASS / WARN / FAIL per skill. Does NOT auto-fix anything.
- standup: Generate a standup update from yesterday's git activity and PR status. Use this whenever you need to prepare a standup message, daily update, or summary of recent work — even if the user just says "what did I do yesterday" or "help me write my standup". Invoke with `/standup` (for yesterday) or `/standup YYYY-MM-DD` (for a specific date).
- standup-global: Generate a standup update from your GitHub activity across ALL repositories — not just the current project. Use this instead of /standup when you work across multiple repos and want a full picture of yesterday's work. Invoke with `/standup-global` (for yesterday) or `/standup-global YYYY-MM-DD` (for a specific date).
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- maestro:docs: Update developer-facing documentation to reflect code changes on the current branch. Runs as an inline skill inside backend-agent and frontend-agent (step 2.5 of the internal sequence) after implementation and before DOD. Receives the explicit list of changed files from the implementation agent. No-op if no public API changes occurred.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
